docs: Uniswap v4 protocol documentation (developers.uniswap.org). Uniswap v4 introduces a singleton PoolManager contract that consolidates all pool state and liquidity management into one contract, a departure from earlier versions' one-contract-per-pool design. The Hooks system lets developers attach programmable extensions that customize pool behavior at specific execution points (beforeSwap, afterSwap, beforeAddLiquidity, etc.). Flash accounting nets all balance changes within a single transaction and settles once at the end via a lock mechanism that ensures atomicity and prevents reentrancy. Token balances inside the PoolManager are represented as ERC-6909 claim tokens, avoiding repeated ERC-20 transfers. Official repositories are v4-core (core pool logic) and v4-periphery (routers, position managers, helpers); an SDK provides programmatic integration. Documented actions include creating pools, swapping, and adding/removing liquidity. Uniswap maintains a dedicated Security Framework for evaluating hook implementations and comprehensive audit documentation. The docs cover concepts, contract references, and a 'Build Your First Hook' guide.
github: github.com/Uniswap/v4-core. Language: Solidity. Dual-licensed under Business Source License 1.1 (BUSL-1.1) and MIT, per-file. Contains core pool logic for creating pools and executing pool actions like swapping and providing liquidity, using a singleton architecture where PoolManager.sol manages all pool state. Testing uses Foundry: test helpers in src/test, tests in test/, with foundry.toml, .solhint.json, and echidna.config.yml (fuzzing/invariant configs) present. The repository has approximately 2.5k stars and 1.3k forks, 1,517 commits on main, 53 open pull requests, and 11 open issues, indicating active development. Released as a public draft for open feedback and community contribution.
token: UNI governance token. Total supply 1,000,000,000 UNI, minted at genesis (September 2020) with a 4-year distribution. At governance launch the treasury was allocated 40% of total UNI supply. UNI holders collectively govern the protocol through delegation and voting; any holder can become a delegate by activating voting rights. Governance controls treasury spending, protocol fee activation (the 'fee switch'), and can mint up to 2% of circulating supply annually after the initial four years. The team allocation vested fully in September 2024. Holding any nonzero UNI and participating in governance grants membership in DUNI, a Wyoming-registered DUNA legal entity established August 2025. The 2025 UNIfication proposal passed with 99.9% support, redirecting over $1.05 billion in fees into a fee-switch-and-burn model.
team: Uniswap Labs, founded by Hayden Adams, who launched Uniswap in November 2018 after being inspired by a blog post from Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin. Adams is Founder & CEO. Leadership includes Mary-Catherine Lader (COO), Chad DePue (VP Engineering), Aseem Sood (Product), Marvin Ammori (Chief Legal Officer), and Callil Capuozzo (Design Lead). Uniswap Labs has 501-1000 employees. A separate Uniswap Foundation funds ecosystem grants and supports governance. The team's UNI allocation fully vested in September 2024. Founder Hayden Adams remains directly involved in governance, submitting fee-switch proposals to final on-chain votes in July 2026.
community: Uniswap governance is active. Roughly 211M UNI (worth several hundred million dollars) is delegated to active voters; executed proposals draw large turnout. 18 million UNI is distributed among 12 key governance delegates, who must maintain at least 80% voting participation for incentives. Governance operates via gov.uniswap.org forum and an on-chain Governor. Recent activity: the UNIfication proposal passed with 99.9% support; in July 2026 founder Hayden Adams sent two proposals to final vote turning on v2/v3 fees on Robinhood Chain and v4 fees across seven networks (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Robinhood, BNB, Polygon, Optimism). Protocol metrics: approximately $3.415 billion total value locked, an annualized fee run-rate of $475M, over $148 billion in 30-day trading volume across 36 chains, with Layer 2 accounting for over 65% of daily volume.
audits: Uniswap v4 is among the most thoroughly reviewed codebases in DeFi, with nine independent audits by OpenZeppelin, Spearbit, Certora, Trail of Bits, ABDK, and Pashov Audit Group. OpenZeppelin identified a critical vulnerability specific to the CELO blockchain in the accounting mechanism arising from complexity updating multiple state variables in edge cases; Trail of Bits identified a low-severity issue where invoking collectFees during a swap interferes with balance tracking. Over 500 researchers took part in a $2.35M security competition in which no critical vulnerabilities were found. Uniswap launched a $15.5M bug bounty for v4 core contracts (the largest in history at the time), administered via Cantina, requiring reports within 24 hours of discovery.
